Definition: the shoulder (proper, i.e. upper end of the arm; as being the spot where the garments hang); figuratively, side-piece or lateral projection of anything
BiblicalUsage: The shoulder is where the burden is carried and the strength is shown, and Aaron bore the names of the sons of Israel on the stones of the ephod on his shoulders, and Benjamin dwells safely because the Lord shall cover him and dwell between his shoulders, and the idol is carried on the shoulder because it cannot walk, and Goliath wore a coat of mail between his shoulders. The word holds the priest, the tribe, the idol, and the giant together, and only one of them carries what it claims.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the shoulder is where God puts the burden and where He gives the strength to carry it. I hold that the idol on the shoulder is the picture of every false god, carried by its worshippers because it cannot carry them, while my God carries me.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
